answer.rationale: The competitor's price attack creates immediate churn pressure on price-sensitive SMB. Promotional_pricing is ruled out: exp_73 showed 30-day retention dropped 12% despite acquisition lift—unsustainable. Referral_incentive works only on established customers (memory_57), not on at-risk, price-sensitive cohorts. Enterprise_sales_assist addresses a different segment. The highest-leverage, lowest-risk option is activation_messaging (memory_91): it improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action. Combined with signup simplification (memory_31, memory_86), activation_messaging targets the core problem—reducing time-to-value and demonstrating product stickiness—rather than competing on price. This addresses churn by improving perceived value and product adoption, not by eroding margins. A standard_experiment on at-risk SMB cohorts using in-product activation messaging can launch this week without verification delay, with clear week-one engagement and 30-day retention metrics as early signals. If successful, it provides a defensible, margin-preserving response to the price attack.
